study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Fraza et al., Nature Mental Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Unraveling the link between CNVs, cognition and individual neuroimaging deviation scores from a population-based reference cohort

nm2_1_modeling_methods.answer: Bayesian Methods: BLR; Bayesian Methods: WBLR
nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study employed Bayesian linear regression (BLR) with likelihood warping (Sinarcsinh function) for normative modeling. This is referred to as warped Bayesian linear regression (WBLR). The PCNtoolkit (version 0.28) was used for all statistical analyses. A cubic B-spline basis expansion with 5 evenly spaced knots was used to capture age-related curvature.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We employed the Bayesian linear regression function from the PCNtoolkit to create the normative models for each voxel; To ensure accurate modeling of nonlinear and non-Gaussian effects, we employed a B-spline basis function and likelihood warping; We employed a Bayesian linear regression model (BLR) with likelihood warping for the normative analysis; This algorithm employed Sinarcsinh likelihood warping and Powell optimization.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Fraza2023.pdf.md: Methods / Normative modeling with Bayesian linear regression; Fraza2023_sup1.pdf.md: Normative model formulation

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Two types of response variables were used: (1) Image-derived phenotypes (IDPs) from UK Biobank including 2,084 IDPs covering structural, functional, and diffusion MR data (global measurements like total brain volume to interregional connectivity). (2) Voxel-wise Jacobian determinants derived from nonlinear image registration to MNI152 space, which measure local volume expansion or contraction (deformation-derived morphometry).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Initially, we fit a normative model to each of the image-derived phenotypes (IDPs) derived from the structural, functional and diffusion measures from the UK Biobank; we aim to explore a whole-brain voxel-based model based on structural T1 data; we fitted a voxel-based morphometric variation model using Jacobian determinant images derived from the nonlinear image registration to the MNI152 space; In total, we used data from 44,456 participants from the UK Biobank and 2,084 IDPs
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Fraza2023.pdf.md: Results; Methods / Normative modeling of IDPs and voxel-based morphometry

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.answer: Age-related: Age; Demographics: Sex; Site/Scanner: Site
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative models used three covariates: age (with B-spline basis expansion for nonlinear effects), sex (binary), and site (as fixed effect to reduce site effects). Site was incorporated as a confounding variable during the fitting procedure.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We created normative models for each individual IDP or voxel, taking into account covariates age, site and sex; Every normative model constructed factored in the covariates age and sex. To reduce site effects, we have added it as a fixed effect in the model; Covariates encompassed age, binary sex, and binary site ID within the covariance matrix; using the covariates age, sex and site
